section: Educational Psychology · Ch7 — Memory, Forgetting & Transfer
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: A student who first memorised their old house's telephone number now finds it hard to remember their NEW phone number because the old memory keeps interfering. This is an example of:

options.option_text: Proactive interference (old learning disrupts new learning)
Retroactive interference (new learning disrupts old learning)

explanation: Proactive interference occurs when OLDER information disrupts the recall of NEWER information — the reverse of retroactive interference, where newly learned material disrupts recall of older material.

section: Educational Psychology · Ch7 — Memory, Forgetting & Transfer
subject: Educational Psychology
stem: Remembering the specific event of your own first day at school (a personal experience tied to a particular time and place) is classified as which type of long-term memory, distinct from memory for general facts?
explanation: Episodic memory stores personally experienced events tied to a specific time/place, while semantic memory stores general facts and knowledge (e.g., 'Paris is the capital of France'), and procedural memory stores learned skills (e.g., riding a bicycle).
